This PR implements direct SharedInformerFactory that is able to serve Lister interface directly from watch cache in a way that is totally transparent to admission. 

Ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142223

Related: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121979 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/121657

/cc @wojtek-t @liggitt 

Admission for pods:

| # | Consumer | Call site | Access pattern | Registers pod event handler? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NodeRestriction admission | [admission.go:119](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/plugin/pkg/admission/noderestriction/admission.go#L119) | `Pods(ns).Get(name)`  | no |
| 2 | PodSecurity admission | [admission.go:121](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/plugin/pkg/admission/security/podsecurity/admission.go#L121) | `ListPods(ctx, ns)`  | no |
| 3 | ResourceClaim quota evaluator | [registry.go:67](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/quota/v1/evaluator/core/registry.go#L67) | `Pods(ns).Get(ownerName)` | no |
| 4 | ServiceAccount token getter | [authentication.go:723](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/kubeapiserver/options/authentication.go#L723) → [tokengetter.go:58](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/controller/serviceaccount/tokengetter.go#L58) | `Pods(ns).Get(name)`, falls back to live client on any error | no |
| 5 | Node authorizer | [config.go:114](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/kubeapiserver/authorizer/config.go#L114) → [graph_populator.go:89](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/node/graph_populator.go#L89) | lister **and** `Informer().AddEventHandler` | **yes** |

Will send a separate PR for rewriting Node Authorizer to use Lister interface.

/kind feature

This is stage 1 out of 2 for removing informers, will add release node in PR that will completly remove apiserver pod informer, but first we would still need to rewrite node authorizer to Lister interface.
```release-note
NONE
```

Thanks @serathius, could we preserve `labels.Nothing()` semantics at the lister boundary here?

At `5b10e94`, `labels.Nothing().Empty()` is `false`, but its `String()` is `""`. `ListWithContext` therefore sends an empty label selector to the direct client, losing the distinction between matching nothing and matching everything.

The existing `cache.ListAll` and `ListAllByNamespace` already short-circuit with `labels.MatchesNothing(selector)`. Would mirroring that guard here, with a test for both the all-namespace and namespaced Pod listers, be appropriate? The test could assert an empty result and no backend call, with `labels.Everything()` as a positive control.

This is source-traced; I haven't run the Kubernetes tests or reproduced a cluster-level failure.

AI-assisted review and draft patch.

Could this be structured more like `Cacher`: same read semantics, different backing source?

`WatchList` used a consistency detector against the old path during rollout, but ideally we wouldn’t need two implementations of filtering/conversion/defaulting to keep in sync.

> /assign @liggitt
> 
> @liggitt - I'm happy to make a deep-dive review, but I remember an attempt of that in the past that you shot down. So I would like to hear your opinion first. [Personally I'm not huge fan of it, but the numbers Marek showed offline imho justify this.]

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121979 was the previous attempt / discussion.

I'm also iffy on this, for basically the same reasons. The risks I see here:

1. We'd now be missing ~everything injected into context by the normal filter chain (especially audit / authn / authz) which storage should be able to rely on
2. Risk of mismatch in how requestinfo is constructed
3. Risk of clients mutating the retrieved objects (either directly or via surprising mutations like [reserialization](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/82497)). This was already a risk, but now the blast radius is changing objects held by the watch cache and returned to all API clients.

edit: I can believe the performance benefits are significant, but it's hard to reason about a second parallel path to getting these objects that doesn't have 100% fidelity (with the context / filters), and with a big blast radius if something unexpected is done with the returned objects.

edit 2: I also think demonstrating how the informer use would be eliminated is important to do before we merge anything in this direction ... if we can't do that, this doesn't actually buy us much, right?

hey all 👋 i did some downstream homework after rereading #142223, trying to understand the allocation problem before contributing allocations to this thread 😅

I went back through @linxiulei’s original prototype and the discussion around it as i’m still learning this stack
my read of @serathius and @jefftree’s investigation is that the opportunity is less informer update/relist work and better recovery, not necessarily cheaper individual reads

my synthetic read benchmark measured ~281 kB/op direct versus ~4.2 kB/op cached for a 100-Pod `List` without `managedFields`. Allocation medians agreed across local and hosted Linux. ofc that’s only one side of the tradeoff & not system-level

the accompanying tests found that current conversion isolates mutations, the selector guard matches client-go, and direct reads retain `managedFields` that informers strip. i also checked context routing and informer lifecycle: the PSA adapter misses the context-aware extension, and event consumers keep the informer alive.

so the hypothesis I wanna test next is whether avoided informer maintenance outweighs added read copying under realistic update/read ratios. that needs equivalent outputs and verified consumer wiring first, then net allocation, retained-memory and recovery measurements.

@enj’s experience with diverging storage/REST paths, and @liggitt/@wojtek-t’s warning about future breakage, helped me understand why these tests passing don't mean much

[Evidence](https://github.com/kvnloo/kubernetes/tree/experiment/direct-lister-contract-142304-20261002)

I used ai assistance (astra) to learn about k8s & carry out the experiments
